guard: a one-shot `cotal send` or `cotal channel` leaves no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
why: Each send used to bind an ordered watch consumer on both buckets. The operator profile cannot
delete it (#691), so it stayed for the five-minute inactive threshold, and a sustained send rate
reached the broker's per-stream consumer ceiling. The suite counts consumers on both streams
before and after three real CLI sends.
The first mutation drops the one-time read from the transient endpoint, which is the shipped
behavior. The other two keep it and put back one watch each in core, so the proof shows the
check sees a leak on either bucket alone. The last one keeps the endpoint's one-time read and
puts back the scan in the channel send's own policy read, which leaked one registry consumer per
channel send. The CLI runs as a subprocess and resolves every package from `dist/`, so each
mutation builds first and rebuilds in `afterRestore`.

mutations.name: the transient endpoint watches again
mutations.expectRed: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.cell: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.note: This is the pre-fix transient: both buckets gain one consumer per send.

mutations.name: a read-once endpoint watches presence
mutations.expectRed: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.cell: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.note: Only the presence stream leaks. It is the watch that binds first, so it is the one the broker refused first in the original report.

mutations.name: a read-once endpoint watches the channel registry
mutations.expectRed: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.cell: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)

mutations.name: `cotal channel` scans the registry with a consumer again
mutations.expectRed: `cotal channel` leaves no consumer on the channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.cell: `cotal channel` leaves no consumer on the channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.note: The pre-fix read: liveKvEntries binds a scan consumer whose delete the operator profile is refused.

mutations.name: a channel send's policy read scans the registry with a consumer again
mutations.expectRed: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.cell: three one-shot sends leave no consumer on the presence or channel-registry stream (#4091)
mutations.note: The release's send: the endpoint read once, but the `-c` send's policy read left one registry consumer.
